thread:
Maya: heads up — product asked for a single dashboard to show GPU capacity health across Hosted + Dedicated pools. Can we align on signals before I sketch a mock?
Sven: +1, we need to decide canonical definitions first. SM occupancy has been used interchangeably with SM utilization in different places.
Kai: quick note: SM occupancy = fraction of warps/threads active on an SM at runtime (useful for kernel-level). SM utilization usually maps to compute vs idle cycles. Which do you want?
Olivia: for high-level dashboards the product wants a single number 'GPU utilization' per pool. I'd prefer occupancy (easy to compute from runtime samples) and call it out in the tooltip.
Dante: important: Dedicated customers expect per-reservation visibility + per-host. Hosted wants aggregated per-region + model-family. We need tags to differentiate pooling.
Maya: proposal: two canonical metrics: 1) redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy (runtime sample, 0..1 gauge) 2) redwood_gpu_memory_allocated_bytes (gauge). Both labeled with pool_type, pool_id, instance_type, model_family, device_id. Thoughts?
Sven: labels sound good but watch cardinality: model_family for Hosted could blow up if we tag with full model id. Maybe limit to model_family and quantization-level only.
Kai: agree. Also add allocation_state tag (idle/active/evicted) for queue depth reasoning.
Olivia: queue depth: do we expose per-device queue_depth (number of in-flight requests queued on that GPU) or per-pool pending_requests? Product wants both.
Dante: we already emit per-worker request counters in the runtime logs. The consumer can aggregate to per-device queue_depth gauge via a rolling sum. We should standardize the computation window (10s sliding).
Maya: let's add spec: queue_depth = sum of requests waiting on device queue over last 10s (gauge), and enqueued_latency_ms histogram. Example name: redwood_gpu_queue_depth.
Sven: alerting proposals? For Dedicated: if avg sm_occupancy > 0.92 for 5m -> no new allocations / notify infra. For Hosted: >0.85 triggers autoscale heuristic.
Kai: careful — sustained high occupancy but low latency could be fine (good batching). I prefer combo alert: 1) high occupancy AND 95th token-latency degradation OR queue_depth growth.
Olivia: UX ask: dashboards should show causal linkage: occupancy -> queue_depth -> latency. Also allow pinning a model_family filter and per-pool drilldown.
Dante: implementation details - telemetry pipeline: runtime emits lightweight metric events every request lifecycle and periodic device samples. Consumer aggregates into Prometheus-compatible timeseries with labels. Need to define ingestion schema.
Maya: I'll draft the schema. Quick example snippet for the telemetry side:```
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy{pool_type="hosted",pool_id="eu-w-1",device_id="gpu-3",model_family="seq2seq-8b"} 0.68
redwood_gpu_memory_allocated_bytes{pool_type="dedicated",reservation_id="r-123",device_id="gpu-1"} 1099511627776
redwood_gpu_queue_depth{pool_type="hosted",pool_id="us-e-2",device_id="gpu-2"} 3
```
Sven: nice. Also include a per-shard sample for cuda_reserved_memory vs process_rss to help diagnose fragmentation. Maybe: redwood_gpu_memory_reserved_bytes and redwood_gpu_memory_used_bytes.
Kai: retention/rollups: raw 1s metrics for 1h, 10s rollups for 7d, 1m rollups for 30d. That keeps cost sane.
Olivia: for Dedicated customers we should keep 1s resolution for 7d at least (they pay for predictability). Can we make retention configurable per-customer?
Dante: yes via telemetry consumer config tied to reservation_id. We'll need a small API change to set retention_policy label.
Maya: UX for rollouts: when we roll a new runtime with different kernel selection, we should mark timeline annotations in the dashboard so we can correlate occupancy shifts. Add label runtime_version to metrics.
Sven: good call. Also add field for scheduling_strategy (e.g., packed vs spread) to help explain occupancy differences.
Kai: metric types: occupancy and memory => gauge. queue_depth => gauge. request_rate => counter (redwood_gpu_requests_total). latency => histogram with prometheus buckets.
Olivia: dashboard layout idea: top row global KPIs (pool-level occupancy p50/p95, total queued), middle row heatmap (device-by-device occupancy), bottom row per-model drilldown and recent anomalies.
Dante: add a small 'dedicated contract' pane showing reservation_id, SLA target, and current headroom percentage. Headroom = (capacity - active_allocations)/capacity.
Maya: headroom calculation agreed. We should surface 'fallback' policy triggers used by routing (e.g., fallback_to_lower_gflops) as an annotation when headroom < threshold.
TelemetryBot: note: current telemetry schema v1.3 does not include model_family label in runtime metrics. Backwards incompatible change — will create migration plan if we add it.
Maya: thanks TelemetryBot. Migration plan idea: emit new labels alongside legacy metrics for 2 weeks, then flip consumers.
Sven: one more operational thing — compute SM occupancy at the kernel level might be noisy. Consider smoothing with exponential moving average (alpha=0.2) at ingestion. Document it clearly.
Kai: agree. Also publish definition doc with pseudo-code showing how occupancy is computed from sampled active_warps / max_warps_per_sm to avoid ambiguity.
Maya: I'll draft the PR with: metric names, types, labels, aggregation windows, rollups, retention tiers, and dashboard mock. Expect it by EOD.
Olivia: copy for product review would be great. I'll add UX notes and mock mockups.
Dante: I'll draft the telemetry consumer changes and a migration runbook for Dedicated customers.
Sven: I'll prepare alerting rules and sample PromQL queries for the dashboard.
Maya: cool — thanks all. Ping me if you see gaps. :+1:
InfraBot: deploy-bot: telemetry-consumer v2.14 scheduled for canary at 2026-04-05T03:00Z
Maya: added the canary to the PR description and linked infra runbook.
Olivia: leaving a small UX note: show exact tooltip definitions on hover with links to the pseudo-code doc.
Kai: one-liner PromQL for occupancy p95 per-pool:```quantile_over_time(0.95, redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy{pool_type="hosted",pool_id="us-e-2"}[5m])```
Sven: tweak: use histogram_quantile with a summary of sampled occupancy if we go that route.
Dante: ok closing loop — I'll sync with infra tomorrow and prepare a test plan that creates synthetic load at varying batch sizes so we can validate occupancy vs latency correlation.
Maya: thanks team — will post the PR link here once ready.
